top_strength: When Andrew flagged that his schedule might shift because he's also selling his house and lining up a second move, Erik didn't brush past it -- 'Hey, that's totally fine Andrew, that's totally fine man. We'll get you squared away and make sure that we can make any movements that we need to with you.' He also ran a genuinely thorough room-by-room inventory before quoting, which is why the estimate (two-day pack/move, $2,653) was grounded in real detail instead of a guess.
coaching_note: You skipped the two highest-value pieces of this call: the Save Your Ass prep speech (worth 10 points and it's the section that actually shrinks the customer's bill) and every one of the differentiators in Section 3 -- No Worries damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee were all completely absent. Open with a real agenda statement instead of jumping straight into confirming the move date, and don't skip address, stairs, storage, and access questions just because some details are pre-populated -- confirm them out loud. Also tighten the pricing walkthrough -- burying the appliance question mid-sentence inside the rate explanation made that part of the call harder to follow than it needed to be.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and used the customer's name often with one genuine empathy moment on the schedule uncertainty, but most of the call was transactional data relay with rambling, unstructured delivery and little rapport beyond the task.
